results.correct_value: The crux is P4, topped by overhanging double corners at 5.10d (5.10+); P8 at 5.10b is the second-hardest; the route is otherwise sustained 5.10a/b. rock_grade should read 5.10d.
results.evidence: The first-ascent report grades the route IV 5.10+ and says the crux fourth pitch is a 5.8 chimney and hard 5.9 offwidth topped by an overhanging 5.10+ double corner. A detailed trip report grades the route IV+ 5.10d. The general description calls it fairly sustained 5.10a/b with the short power crux in the double overhanging corners on the chimney pitch, so '5.10a/b' is the route's character, not its maximum; P4 at 5.10d is right and rock_grade 5.10b was the outlier (one older forum TR title said 5.10b).

results.fact: Which way the route faces (aspect E / 'East face of Whine Spire' vs seasonal_guidance 'the cold west face')
results.evidence: aspect is E, face and overview say east face, and the approach variant traverses beneath the east faces from the far side of Burgundy Col, but seasonal_guidance July and September both say 'west face'. The first-ascent report places the route on 'the west face of Silver Star Mountain' (the massif's west side, not necessarily the spire's own aspect), while another description calls Whine Spire a sub-peak on the east face of Silver Star. Settling it needs two sources that state the aspect of the Gato Negro wall itself.

results.fact: Direction of the Option B traverse to the south ridge
results.correct_value: A rising traverse from the meadow to the level part of the south ridge at about 6,180 ft, with no eastward direction: the pullout lies east/southeast of the summit, so the ridge cannot be reached by traversing east.
results.evidence: The route description for this line says to park at the turnout about 3.1 mi east of Rainy Pass (0.7 mi before Blue Lake TH), take the boot path through a meadow and make a rising traverse to the level part of the south ridge at 6,180 ft - it gives no direction. The peak's own coordinate (48.5155, -120.7079) with SR-20 bending around its southern base puts that pullout east/southeast of the summit, so an eastward traverse leads away from the south ridge. The unsourced word 'east' is removed from both copies; no new direction is asserted.
